clue.text: Birds show pleasure endlessly, finding flowering plant

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the purring word is dropped

parts.note: a contented cat purrs to show pleasure

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's delight in the garden ends with spotting a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a delphinium-like garden plant with spurred blue flowers, so it is an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Old stringed instrument storyteller talked of

indicators.note: spoken about, so the word for the fibber is heard rather than written

parts.note: someone who tells stories, i.e. fibs, is a liar

explanation.surface: A bard is remembered for the ancient harp he played while telling tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storyteller' looks like a bard, which fits the instrument, but here it means someone who tells lies.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is a small harp of ancient Greece, plucked to accompany song.

clue.text: Bakery product — or part, so it's said

indicators.note: signals that the word for an actor's part is heard, not spelt

parts.note: an actor's part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A baker offers a loaf or a piece of one, by repute.
explanation.definitionFit: A bread roll is a small individual loaf sold by bakers.

clue.text: Slovenly former nurse drinking coffee extremely languidly

indicators.note: the nurse takes the coffee in, so it goes inside her letters

parts.note: SRN, State Registered Nurse, is an old British nursing qualification
a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the following word

explanation.surface: A scruffy retired nurse lounges about sipping coffee very lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: SRN (State Registered Nurse) was a British qualification no longer awarded, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatternly describes a person who is untidy and dirty in habits, just as slovenly does.

clue.text: Put out about biography finally lacking spiritual elevation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the shortened biography word
put out in the sense of disordered, so the three letters of the word put are rearranged
missing its last letter, so the end of the word for a biography goes

parts.note: a biography is a life story, a life

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed that a memoir lacks inspiring moral uplift at its close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as annoyed, but 'out' is the anagram signal, making UPT, and 'about' wraps that round the shortened biography.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplift is a feeling of being morally or spiritually raised up, an improving elevation of the spirit.

clue.text: Clothing to boast about

indicators.note: turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: Someone's outfit is something to show off about.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for dress or attire, especially of a distinctive kind.

clue.text: Cow possibly turned up Japanese coin under tree

indicators.note: in a down entry the coin part sits below the tree

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upward means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the yen is Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A cow may be found grazing beneath a tree where someone found a Japanese coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks the definition as an example: Alderney is a breed of dairy cattle, named after a Channel Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is a breed of dairy cattle from the Channel Islands, so a cow may be one.

clue.text: Couple allowed to make wrist ornament

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means permitted

explanation.surface: A pair are permitted to craft a piece of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band or chain of jewellery worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Soldiers apt to be trustworthy

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
apt to do something means liable to do it

explanation.surface: Troops who are inclined to behave can be relied upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliable means dependable, able to be trusted.

clue.text: English theologian introducing a collection of old Norse poems

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theology degree

explanation.surface: An English scholar of divinity presents an anthology of ancient Scandinavian verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is the medieval Icelandic compilation of Norse mythological and heroic poetry.

clue.text: Untruthfulness of woman in popular financial area

indicators.note: the woman's name goes inside the other letters

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the City is London's financial district
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman working in a fashionable banking district is accused of lying.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the Square Mile of London where the big banks sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness; adding the negative prefix gives lying or dishonesty.

clue.text: Hospital worker fastens fur badly

indicators.note: done badly, so the letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily does up a fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a staff nurse is a registered nurse ranking below a sister.

clue.text: Bitter syrup produced by Missouri girls

parts.note: MO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Missouri
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Some girls from Missouri make a sharp-tasting syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark, slightly bitter syrup left over from refining sugar.

clue.text: Bookish boss with evidence of debts

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: A scholarly employer keeps a record of what he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but means an ornamental knob, a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious means given to study and reading, which is what bookish means.

clue.text: Protest about being trapped in blooming railway!

indicators.note: the about letter sits enclosed by the other letters

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
C, circa, means about

explanation.surface: People complain about being stuck on a flipping railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild swear word but means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public complaint or protest.

clue.text: Go back and surrender again

definitions.meaning: re- plus cede, to give up once more

explanation.definitionFit: Recede means to move back or retreat; split as re-cede it means to yield up a second time.

clue.text: A new star beginning to look like stars generally

indicators.note: made new, so the letters are rearranged into a fresh order
the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A newly appearing star starts to look like the rest of the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is an adjective meaning relating to or resembling the stars.

clue.text: Spanish youth rejected by an upper-class Welsh girl

indicators.note: sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth
U is the conventional label for upper-class usage
Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A young man from Spain is spurned by a posh girl from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Andalusian means from Andalusia, the southern region of Spain, so it is a kind of Spanish.

clue.text: Festive gathering a local leader established in Georgia

indicators.note: the leading, first, letter of the following word

clue.text: Advantage admitted by landed gentry

indicators.note: let in by, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a slight advantage over a rival, as in having the edge.

clue.text: Flat-bottomed boat made by firm in the Devon area

parts.note: Devon lies in the south-west of England, SW

explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in the far south-west of England.

clue.text: Dinar Don changed for would-be priest?

clue.text: Symbol of rank crack troops held at first

indicators.note: the first letter of the preceding word

parts.note: PE, physical education, means exercise
